text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Hydro-Quebec denies profit figure: Utility says it's not making the C$750 million that Newfoundland claims.
- Push is on to finish Toronto's Sheppard subway line: Metro to be told 'Just do it.'

- Killing of seal pups probed: Federal officials are in the final stages of investigating reports that whitecoat and blueback seal pups were slaughtered and processed this year at a Newfoundland plant during a federally subsidized seal hunt in which 260,000 mammals were killed.
- Ontario's ruling Conservatives stall bid to oust legislative speaker: Members of Provincial Parliament want to see report on sexual harassment complaint against Al McLean.
- Fetus endured 'sleep-room' experiments: Man denied compensation claim for brainwashing conducted in 1960 on his mother.
- U.S. Federal Reserve holds line on U.S. rates: Canadian rates also likely to stay put as chairman Alan Greenspan resists pressure from regional banks.
- Robert Friedland loses surprise bid to unlock assets: Financier appears in Ontario court to fight U.S. freeze.
- Consumers Distributing Inc's customers wooed: Retailers chase bankrupt chain's shoppers with aggressive ads.
- iStar Internet Inc bolsters position amid Internet shuffling: Bank of Nova Scotia agrees to take ten percent stake.
- No retreat on Canada Pension Plan reform, Ottawa says: British Columbia's objections too late to stop changes, Liberals contend.
- Joy short-lived as Fed holds rates.
- Former Scott's Hospitality Inc CEO picked to run WIC Western International Communications Inc.
